ctx.x: Did they have bands around Spring Hill College? Did you have a college band?

Oh, yes. The first band that I played with in Mobile, the trumpet player was Joe Walsh. Joe Walsh and I went to Spring Hill together. He was, without a doubt, the most superstitious person that you ever saw in your life. And when we'd go to Fairhope, we'd play on the ferry all the way from Mobile to Fairhope across Mobile Bay. And that's the way we got over there, by playing. We got transportation. Then we'd go and play at the casino for the Funk Brothers at Fairhope. And then that was in the afternoon. Then that…

items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-08-01
items.q: That was in the first band I played in, in Atmore, Alabama. We went up there. One of the boys were in the band. Bobby Swartz was in love with a girl up there.

ctx.x: Yeah. We were talking about your being on the road in places like Texas. Did you ever stay in private homes?

Once in a great while we'd play a big affair at a private home and stay there that night. Homes big enough all up in northern Alabama and all over everywhere. Atmore, Alabama, we did that. That was in the first band I played in, in Atmore, Alabama. We went up there. One of the boys were in the band. Bobby Swartz was in love with a girl up there. And her family invited us to come up there to a big fried chicken dinner. And we sat down to the table and there was just stacks and stacks and stacks of fried chicken on…
And generally, how was the food on the road? You mentioned having to eat hot dogs.
